text:
Erik Gustafsson has played for ten NHL teams, and in Los Angeles this month he has looked at home. He missed three games, came back on Nov. 17 in Boston with a goal and an assist, and now has a four-game point streak (1 goal, 5 assists).

At 34, he is playing 20 minutes a night and leading the Kings' power play from the point: 5 of his 9 points in 15 games have come with the man advantage. His ice time over the last ten games is up 4.4 minutes. Los Angeles gets 57% of the expected goals at five-on-five with him on, 7.7 points better than without him.

Some of this is a hot run. He has 2 goals on 13 shots, a 15.4% shooting rate against a range of about 5% to 9% for him, and he is scoring 1.79 points per 60 against a talent range of 0.9 to 1.9. The range is wide because he played only two games last season, with Detroit. What is real is the role: as long as he runs the power play, the points have a floor.
headline: A journeyman on a heater
